value.rationale: For positive-ambiguity multiwindow inverse formulas, the smallest weighted denominator over a specified observation disk is a directly motivated worst-case division margin. This theorem exactly optimizes its angular design across every pair of fixed positive weights and genuinely squeezed Gaussians, proves complete equality rigidity, and identifies an explicit radius where the worst-case direction splits from one line to two. The threshold is a natural configuration boundary rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; the work makes no claim about overall inverse error or sampled uniqueness.
